subject: literature
passage: On the last night the cinema was open, Mr. Haddad climbed to the projection booth an hour early, as he had every evening for forty-one years. He had already chosen the film. Mr. Haddad, squinting at a strip of it held up to the ______ could still name the scene from the pattern of its frames, the way a sailor reads weather from the shape of a cloud. Downstairs, a few dozen people settled into the worn seats. When the lights went down, he let the first frames flicker across the screen and allowed himself, for once, to watch.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Squinting at a strip of it held up to the light" is extra information describing what Mr. Haddad was doing. It opens with a comma after "Haddad," so it must close with a comma before the verb "could still name."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "could still name."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Mr. Haddad" from its verb "could still name."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The extra information opens with a comma, so it can't close with a dash; the two marks must match.
explanation.D: Correct. The closing comma matches the opening comma after "Haddad" and completes the pair around the extra information.
